fieldMarks: Chocolate to dark brown fur with irregular white patches on the chin, throat and belly (usually larger on females).
Long body, short legs and semi-webbed toes.
Oily guard hairs make the coat water-resistant.
Males are substantially larger than females; males roughly 19–29 in long and 3–5 lb.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal, especially near dawn and dusk; movements are quick and erratic.
Solitary; marks territory with anal-gland secretions and can discharge a foul-smelling liquid when threatened.
Strong swimmer that dives to about 5 m; dens in riverbank burrows or dens taken over from other mammals.
Eats crayfish and frogs in summer and small mammals (including muskrats), fish and waterfowl year-round, with mammals dominating winter diet.
habitat: Closely tied to water: streams, ponds, lakes, marshes, lake shores and saltwater beaches, especially forested or brushy shorelines with cover.
range: Native across most of Canada and every US state except Arizona. Escaped fur-farm mink are established outside North America, including the British Isles.
